question.problem: Consider the surface $x{y}^{2}+6=z{x}^{2}.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(-2,-1,1).$

current_example.problem: Consider the surface $z^3y^2 =x^2-5.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to this surface at the point $(-1,2,-1).$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{3}{y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-5 \\ {z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2} & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z) = z^3y^2 - x^2,$ our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-5.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

$$
\nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle  = 0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(-1,2,-1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =(-2x)\text{ }i+2{z}^{3}y\text{ }j+3{z}^{2}{y}^{2}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(-1,2,-1) & =(-2)(-1)\text{ }i+2(-1)^{3}(2)\text{ }j+3(-1)^{2}(2)^{2}\text{ }k \\  & =2\,i-4j+12\,k \\  & =⟨2,-4,12⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,2,-1)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),\,y-2,\,z-(-1)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,-4,12⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-2,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ 2(x+1)-4(y-2)+12(z+1) & =0 \\ 2x-4y+12z+22 & =0 \\ x-2y+6z+11 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
